title: United States and United Kingdom strike Houthi targets in Yemen
body:
On 12 January 2024, the United States and the United Kingdom launched strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen in response to the group's attacks on Red Sea shipping. US Lieutenant General Douglas Sims said the strikes hit nearly 30 locations using more than 150 munitions. They were the first strikes on Yemeni territory by the US since 2016. The US said Australia, Bahrain, Canada and the Netherlands supported the operation.

President Joe Biden called them targeted strikes and said he would not hesitate to take further action if necessary. UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak called them necessary and proportionate. White House spokesperson John Kirby said the US was not seeking a war with Yemen. The Houthis' Supreme Political Council said all American-British interests had become legitimate targets, and the Houthis said the strikes killed five people, a figure Al Jazeera did not independently confirm.

Houthi-run Al Masirah named targets including an air base north of Sanaa, Hodeidah airport, a camp east of Saada, Taiz airport and an airport near Hajjah. Iran condemned the attacks, and Russia requested an urgent UN Security Council meeting. The strikes followed a UN Security Council resolution on 11 January condemning Houthi attacks. Tens of thousands of Yemenis rallied in several cities against the strikes.
